elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised (h): "provided however, that Customer may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets..." — the no-consent affiliate route is expressly retained for Customer.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised (h) preserves "purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction" as a no-consent route for Customer; merger, stock-sale acquisition and asset sale are all covered.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening prohibition "Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) ... without the other Party's prior written consent" is retained, and the sole no-consent exception is now limited to Customer, so Kubient has no unconsented assignment route.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained existing language: "without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "Kubient may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Customer" — an absolute bar, not merely a consent condition.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "no change of control of Customer shall give Kubient any right to terminate this Agreement"; paragraph 4 contains no competing change-of-control trigger, so no retained contradiction.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: As revised, only Customer holds the no-consent successor route; Kubient's successor assignment remains gated by the "Neither Party may assign ... without the other Party's prior written consent" sentence, so the right is no longer mutual. To reach fallback the drafter would have to restore mutuality ("either Party") for successor transfers.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained nor the added language imposes any notice obligation on a permitted successor assignment; a written-notice requirement would have to be inserted expressly.

The retained Customer affiliate exception is a no-consent, non-successor exception ("may assign ... without approval or consent to any affiliate"), which under the rule boundaries defeats a blanket "other assignments require consent" outcome.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" applies to all non-excepted assignments.

reasons: Preferred level is complete in operative text: the no-consent carve-out is narrowed to Customer only (affiliate, substantially-all-assets purchaser, merger/stock-sale/consolidation successor), the mutual consent gate with the reasonableness standard is retained and now binds Kubient alone in practice, and the appended sentence supplies both the competitor bar and the express no-change-of-control-termination confirmation.

Fallback is not complete (successor mutuality, written notice, and a clean consent-for-all-others rule all fail), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation from the fallback in the original text.

Edits are confined to the checklist: two substitutions inside the proviso ("either Party"->"Customer", "said Party's"->"Customer's") and one concise added sentence covering the two remaining preferred elements. No survival tails, procedures, notwithstanding override, or extra requirements were added, and the favourable existing reasonableness standard, void-attempt sentence and successors-and-assigns sentence are retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved: no new Vendor assignment exception was created, no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling, and the added change-of-control sentence does not contradict paragraph 4, which contains only material-breach, insolvency and post-Initial-Term 90-day termination triggers (none keyed to change of control).

Drafting note (non-blocking): the successor carve-out remains limited by the pre-existing "assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement" qualifier; leaving it intact is the minimal choice, and it does not defeat the element.
